ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is triangle XYZ, X is at the lower left, Z is at the lower right, Y is above; point M is on side XY, point N is on side XZ; line segment MN and side YZ have the same arrow marks, indicating MN ∥ YZ. Then reason: It is known that XM = 4, XN = 6, NZ = 9, so XZ = XN + NZ = 6 + 9 = 15. Because MN ∥ YZ, triangle XMN is similar to triangle XYZ. The corresponding sides are XM ↔ XY, XN ↔ XZ, therefore XM/XY = XN/XZ. Substituting gives 4/XY = 6/15. Cross-multiplying: 6·XY = 4·15 = 60, so XY = 10.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a triangle XYZ where MN is drawn from point N on base XZ to point M on side XY, with MN parallel to YZ. From the text, XN = 6 and NZ = 9, so the base is split in the ratio XN:NZ = 6:9 = 2:3. By the side-splitter theorem, the parallel segment divides side XY in the same ratio, so XM:MY = 2:3. Since XM = 4 represents the 2 parts, one part is 2, so MY = 3 parts = 6. Therefore XY = XM + MY = 4 + 6 = 10.

推理：因为 MN ∥ YZ，所以由平行线分线段成比例定理，底边被分成的比例 XN:NZ 等于边 XY 上对应部分的比例 XM:MY。已知 XN = 6，NZ = 9，所以 XN:NZ = 6:9 = 2:3。因此 XM:MY = 2:3。又已知 XM = 4，对应 2 份，所以 1 份 = 2，MY 对应 3 份，即 MY = 6。于是 XY = XM + MY = 4 + 6 = 10。
